sents.d: Direct outreach and existing networks often work faster than waiting to be found.

New freelance writers often wait passively for clients to find them, but direct, personalized outreach to businesses that clearly need writing help (an outdated blog, thin website copy) tends to produce faster results.

Freelance job platforms can provide early volume and reviews, though rates are often lower — treating early platform work as a stepping stone to direct clients, rather than a permanent strategy, keeps expectations realistic.

Letting your existing network know specifically what kind of writing work you do — not just a vague 'I'm freelancing now' post — makes it much easier for people to think of you when a relevant need comes up.

take: Pitch businesses that clearly need writing, and tell your network.
